sections.title: Reading Comprehension · Passage B
sections.intro: Read “Bats and Swallows” and answer questions 10–14.

questions.prompt: Lines 1 through 6 introduce the idea that the “we” are

choices.text: unaware of the presence of the creatures
unmoved by the behavior of the creatures

questions.explanation: The speakers can see that the creatures have wings but cannot tell whether they are swallows or bats (lines 1–6). They are watching informally, not identifying the animals as experts.
Lines 6–9 mention wings and small pointed shapes swooping through the air. These visible features fit either swallows or bats, which is why the speakers cannot decide between them.

questions.prompt: Which phrase contributes to the understanding of the word “gloaming” (line 10)?
questions.explanation: “Gloaming” refers to twilight or dusk. The earlier phrase “soft shadows” gives a clue that the light is dim, making choice 1 the phrase that helps explain the word.

questions.prompt: The use of imagery in lines 8 through 15 is meant to portray the narrator’s observation as
questions.explanation: The narrator describes the creature as almost “iridescent” and follows its “crescent” flight across the hill. These shimmering, graceful images make the sight feel beautiful rather than threatening or ordinary.

questions.prompt: The use of the phrase “that either, or both, hold sway” (line 30) shows that

choices.text: each companion is angry with the other
each companion believes the other is mistaken
the narrator is choosing to ignore the evidence
the narrator believes no firm decision is necessary

questions.explanation: The narrator accepts that the animals could be swallows, bats, or both. Because the speakers lack enough evidence to know for sure, the narrator is comfortable leaving the question open rather than forcing a decision.
